# dsh-desk-card

Bottom-right native desktop cards for **DSH (DeepSeek Harness)** approvals, questions, turn
completi

ative desktop cards for **DSH (DeepSeek Harness)** approvals, questions, turn
completion and errors.

Each card is a small always-on-top window drawn by PowerShell/WPF — not a system toast — so it
can c

arry a button that answers the request. An approval can be allowed straight from the card,
and the m

oment a card would interrupt something else (a fullscreen app, a game, Do-Not-Disturb)
it is skipped
and the decision goes back to the normal DSH UI.
Windows only. No dependencies, no network, no build step.
## Why not just a toast
| | system toast | this card |
| carries a button that returns an answer | depends on the shell / extra runtime | yes, the card's o

wn button |
| can allow an approval in place | no (toasts only focus the app) | yes — `确认允许` / `Allo

w` |
| respects fullscreen games and Do-Not-Disturb | only if the OS suppresses it | explicit gate,

checked before the window is drawn |
| UI language | whatever the OS shows | follows the DSH locale,
or forced with `language` |
## Screenshots
## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 (cards are drawn with `powershell.exe` + WPF, which ship with Windows).
- DSH deskto

p profile (the cards are injected by the **host** process, no browser side needed).
- Node.js 20+ (w
hatever DSH ships is fine).
## Install
From this repository:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or from a local clone / download:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then restart DSH. The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so the CLI records it in
`dsh.profile.bundles`
and mounts it as a normal profile layer — no hand-written paths.

Windows developer helper: `powershell.exe -File tools/deploy-local.ps1` copies the working tree
into
`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\plugins\dsh-desk-card` and registers it the same way.
## What shows up
| card | when | auto-close | buttons |
| Approval | a tool call needs permission | never (waits for you) | `确认允许` / `Allow` approves once ·

clicking the card opens DSH for the full dialog |
| Question | the agent asks you something | never

, closes when the question is answered | `知道了` / `Got it` |
| Completion | a turn ends normally | `d

oneTimeoutSeconds` (default 5s) | `知晓` / `OK` |
| Error | a turn fails | never | `知道了` / `Got it` |

The completion card also carries a short summary of your last message, the elapsed time, the
remaini
ng todo count and the turn/session token usage.

Cards never overlap: a new card stacks above the ones already on screen. If the DSH window is
closed
while a card is open, the card closes itself too.
## Configuration

Everything has a built-in default, so this section is optional. To change something, add a row
with
the same id from your profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Only the keys you list are changed — a `config` object replaces the whole object, and every key
you
leave out falls back to the defaults below.
| key | default | meaning |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `0` | auto-close seconds for cards that wait for **you** (approval / question).

`0` = stay until answered |
| `doneTimeoutSeconds` | `5` | auto-close seconds for the completion ca

rd. `0` = keep it until clicked |
| `scale` | `1.2` | card scale factor |
| `skipWhenFullscreen` | `
true` | skip cards while a fullscreen app is in the foreground, or while Windows says Do-Not-Disturb

|
| `notifyQuestions` | `true` | show the question card |
| `notifyErrors` | `true` | show the erro

r card |
| `notifyDone` | `true` | show the completion card |
| `language` | `auto` | `auto` (follow

the DSH locale), `zh` or `en` |
| `hostProcess` | `DeepSeek Harness` | the process whose window is
brought to front when you click a card |

The three `notify*` switches only control the cards — approvals and questions always keep
working, t
he card just does not appear.
### The fullscreen gate
A card is not drawn when either of these is true:

- `SHQueryUserNotificationState` reports a fullscreen app, presentation mode or Do-Not-Disturb; or
-

the foreground window covers its whole monitor and is not the desktop (this keeps games that
hide t
he real state from being interrupted).

When a card is skipped the approval is handed back to the normal DSH UI (with `prepend: true`
this p

lugin speaks first, and a skipped card always delegates to the next answerer), so nothing
gets stuck
. Two test tools reproduce the condition without a game:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Exit-code protocol between the two halves:
| code | meaning |

| `10` | the card's primary button was pressed |
| `12` | the card body was clicked — bring the DSH

window to the front, let the UI decide |
| `0` | gate skipped the card (fullscreen / Do-Not-Disturb)

|
| `3` | rendering failed |

Being one process per card keeps the render half stateless: a card can never wedge the host,
and a c
ard that is killed by the OS just delegates the decision.
## Limitations

- Windows only. The render half is PowerShell + WPF; there is no macOS/Linux path.
- Cards are ordin

ary top-level windows, so they appear above other windows but not above a
fullscreen exclusive game

— which is why the gate exists.
- One PowerShell process per card (about 100 ms of warm-up). A card

is not a notification
center entry: once it is closed it is gone.
- This plugin deliberately does **

not** restart or shut down DSH. If you want power controls,
dsh-power-button and
dsh-restart do that

restart or shut down DSH. If you want power controls,
dsh-power-button and
dsh-restart do that well.
## Privacy

The host half never opens a socket and never reads a file. It spawns one local PowerShell
process pe

r card and appends a line to `%TEMP%\dsh-desk-card.log`. Card payloads contain short
excerpts of you

r session (task title, tool name, approval reason, error message) and are passed
to that child proce
ss as a command-line argument.
